summary: Malheur County, OR lookout on BLM land: 1958 firefinder, cabin about 1965, staffed to 1963; removed with no date. No source describes the summit today.

facts.design: 1958 firefinder with trailer living quarters; cabin about 1965, wood frame, 15 ft 6 in square, on a concrete slab
facts.status_note: firelookout.com says gone; the Rex page says removed, with no date given

events.note: Earliest known use: a temporary lookout on Monument Peak in the 1958 fire season (newspaper, August 28, 1958); firelookout.com lists a firefinder and trailer quarters that year and Mr. and Mrs. Lloyd Edmunson as 1958-1959 personnel
Clara Powell and Altha Hill were working the station for the BLM in summer 1963, per a July 18, 1963 Record-Courier item
Wood-frame cabin, 15'6" square, on a concrete slab; date is approximate (c.1965)

evidence.supports: 1958 firefinder with trailer living quarters; cab in the 1960s; gone
evidence.quote: 1958: firefinder, trailer living quarters. 1960s: cab. Gone.

evidence.supports: Mr. and Mrs. Lloyd Edmunson listed as lookout personnel 1958-1959
evidence.quote: Known lookout personnel: 1958-1959: Mr. & Mrs. Lloyd Edmunson.

evidence.supports: August 1958 newspaper: two temporary lookouts that fire season, one on Monument Peak east of Juntura
evidence.quote: August 28, 1958: Two temporary fire lookouts are watching over a wide area this fire season. One is on Lookout Mountain in the Baker district. The other is on Monument Peak east of Juntura.
June 13, 1963: Clara Powell and Altha Hill will be on a lookout on Monument, 17 miles from Juntura.

evidence.supports: summer 1963 station worked by Clara Powell and Altha Hill for BLM (Record-Courier, July 1963)
evidence.quote: July 18, 1963: Mrs. Clara Powell and grandsons John and Jesse Powell, Enreprise, were here Saturday. Clara is working with Altha Hill of Unity, on Monument Lookout station near Juntura, for BLM this summer.

evidence.supports: cabin c.1965, wood frame, 15 ft 6 in square, on concrete slab
evidence.quote: c.1965: A 15'6" x 15'6" wood frame lookout cabin built on a concrete slab floor.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A June 1963 newspaper item says 17 miles from Juntura. The 1965 survey note gives about 11 miles southeast, and its directions cite a 10-mile sign. The story reports both figures without choosing one.

notes_for_editor: Brief record checks out: BLM, Malheur County, status gone. Two other Oregon Monument Peaks exist (Linn County, 44.69848 -122.32734, FFLOS US 978; and the Rex page's Linn County entry); do not merge. Access is unknown and no current access source was found. Staffing dates come from newspapers and one personnel list. The 1965 survey mark is on the southern, highest of the Jones Buttes about 30 ft northeast of the lookout, not at the peak's highest point, so the story says so. The 2015 Ron Kemnow photo credit on the Rex page has no image URL, so no photo was added. The one web search returned only a Montana Monument Peak, which was not used.
